messages:
lina-cs: FYI onboarding call with Nimbus just finished. Their web integration fails only from corporate network: 403 on /v1/chat when using ephemeral browser tokens. Works from mobile and home network.

devon-eng: classic middlebox behavior. ask for a curl -v from inside corp network showing both request headers and response. proxies sometimes drop Authorization or rewrite Host which breaks aud checks. also confirm if the 403 body is our 'invalid_scope' or 'aud_mismatch' text.

sam-platform: two additional probes: 1) have them run jwt.io decode on the ephemeral token and paste aud/scope (they can redact user/email); 2) check for any transparent proxy insertion like 'Proxy-Authorization' or 'X-Forwarded-For' that some corp security appliances add and then enforce stricter auth.

lina-cs: they provided a sanitized curl: ```curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer ey...redacted" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden content-type: application/json {"error":"invalid_scope","message":"token lacks scope: chat.create"} ``` They insist scope is present.

devon-eng: if scope claim is present and outside network works, then something between their machines and our edge is modifying token or header-casing. ask them to run: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat``` and paste the client-side raw request log. That will show if the token is truncated or wrapped.

sam-platform: also ask for packet capture (or tcpdump) if allowed, to see TLS SNI and if corp TLS terminator is doing re-encrypt + substituting certs. That can change issuer/aud semantics. If they can't share pcap, ask for traceroute to our edge and the cert chain in the failure response.

lina-cs: i've requested: 1) curl -v from corp and from remote, 2) redacted JWT claims, 3) response cert chain and any request-id header. i'll follow up.

onboard-bot: Quick link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdks/browser#proxy-compatibility — has checklist for corp proxies, header-casing, and disabling preflight coalescing via REDWOOD_PREFLIGHT_DISABLE.

devon-eng: one more note: if their SPA uses a service worker or local proxy, that can strip Authorization on fetch for cross-origin. they should test with a plain curl from a terminal on the same machine to rule that out.

lina-cs: great, thanks — keeping this active. will post back with artifacts. :thumbsup:
